title: Service account password expired
symptom: An overnight job stopped running because the account it uses has an expired password
user_description: The nightly report job failed with a logon error. I think its service account password expired over the weekend. Can you look into it?

options.text: Run the job using your own account so it works tonight
options.why: Ties a system job to a person's account, and it breaks again when your password changes or you leave.

options.text: Quietly set the account's password to never expire, without approval
options.why: Changes security policy without permission and does not update the places where the old password is stored.

options.text: Turn the job off so the errors stop
options.why: The report still does not run, and the business is left without it.

options.text: Confirm it in the logs (logon failure for the service account), then escalate to the team that owns the account so the password is updated everywhere it is used
options.why: Service account passwords are stored in services and scheduled tasks. The owning team must change it and update every place it is used.

hints: What does the error in the log say?
Who owns service accounts and the jobs that use them?
Where else might that old password be stored?
real_world_tip: Many companies now use managed service accounts, where Windows changes the password automatically so this cannot happen.

escalation.team_why: Service accounts and the jobs that run on servers belong to the server team. They can change the password and update every service and scheduled task that uses it.

details.text: Which job or app stopped (the nightly report job)

details.why: Shows how long reports have been missing and matches the expiry date.

details.text: The logon failure error from the log
details.why: Proves the cause is the account, not the job itself.

details.text: The new password, written in the ticket
details.why: Never write passwords in tickets. The server team sets and stores it securely.

details.text: Your own password, so they can test with it
details.why: Never share your password, and a person's account should not run system jobs.
